leads.posting: Quanfluence Raises $10 Mn To Build Full-Stack Photonic Quantum Computer. Bengaluru-based quantum compute startup Quanfluence has raised $10 Mn (around ₹92 Cr) in a funding round led by Chiratae Ventures, with participation Rainmatter by Zerodha and existing backer Pi Ventures. Quanfluence plans to deploy the fresh capital to further develop its full-stack photonic quantum computing system, bringing together indigenously designed photonic chips, control electronics and software into a single architecture. The startup is targeting early processors by 2027, followed by larger and scalable quantum machines by 2029. Founded in 2021 by Sujoy Chakravarty, Ravi Mehta, Biman Chattopadhyay, Aditi Vaidya, Anil Prabhaka, and Sandeep Goyal, Quanfluence is building a universal photonic quantum computer and has deployed a quantum-inspired optical Ising machine. The IIT-Madras incubated startup’s core technology includes an optical Ising machine that uses light waves as computational units. The system can process hundreds of interconnected variables simultaneously, making it 100X faster than traditional optimisation methods. Chakravarty told Inc42 that Quanfluence has already commercialised its optical Ising machine, selling the physical systems to customers as well as offering remote access to the machines on a usage-based model. The startup has sold around three machines and currently runs paid pilots with 10-15 corporations. The approach could help Quanfluence generate commercial traction while it works on the significantly harder problem of building a scalable universal quantum computer. The startup’s immediate challenge, however, is less about proving the underlying concept and more about integrating its components, scaling manufacturing and navigating long chip-production and hardware-delivery cycles. With a current team size of 25 employees, it is expecting to scale their workforce to 40-member team over the next year. Previously, Quanfluence raised $2 Mn (around ₹16.7 Cr) i

leads.posting: Zomint raises Rs 36 Cr seed round from Lightspeed and Prime Venture Partners. Wealth management startup Zomint has raised Rs 36 crore ($3.75 million) in a seed round from Lightspeed and Prime Venture Partners. The proceeds will be used to expand its wealth and investment teams, strengthen its technology platform and build its investor education ecosystem. Founded in September 2025 by Aman Mittal and Shavir Bansal, Zomint offers wealth management services to working professionals and families. Investors can start with a monthly SIP of Rs 25,000 or a lump sum investment of Rs 5 lakh. Zomint assigns each family a personal wealth expert who tracks their investments and financial goals. The expert is supported by investment research and AI tools that bring together portfolio information, past conversations and research, flag areas that need attention and track agreed actions. The firm claims it has retained 97% of its clients since launch, despite market volatility. Nearly one in three clients made additional investments through the platform within three months of their initial engagement. Its relationship managers currently serve more than 250 families each, supported by investment specialists and AI enabled tools. Zomint acquired its customers entirely through organic content, using the founders’ financial content platform Bekifaayati, which has more than 50 lakh subscribers.
